item.title: Archaeologists Believe They’ve Discovered The Earliest-Known Evidence Of Fire Made By Humans
item.description: Two little pieces of pyrite, also known as "fool's gold," that were unearthed at the Barnham archaeological site are the "smoking gun" proving that early humans were intentionally making fire as far back as 400,000 years ago. The post Archaeologists Believe They’ve Discovered The Earliest-Known Evidence Of Fire Made By Humans appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: Researchers Just Discovered A New Prehistoric Sea Cow Species That Lived 21 Million Years Ago
item.description: The now-extinct sea cow species, Salwasiren qatarensis, likely played a key role in its ocean ecosystems, much like modern-day dugongs. The post Researchers Just Discovered A New Prehistoric Sea Cow Species That Lived 21 Million Years Ago appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: An Ancient Construction Site In Pompeii Is Revealing How The Romans Made ‘Self-Healing’ Concrete
